stem: The renal artery is derived from which of the following blood vessels:
fact: The renal arteries arise from the abdominal aorta, inferior to the superior mesenteric artery.
mnemonic: Renal arteries arise from the aorta.
finding: NCBI confirms the renal arteries arise from the abdominal aorta.

stem: A 54 year old man presents to ED complaining of abdominal pain radiating to his back. Imaging shows a tumour at the neck of the pancreas. Which of the following structures would first receive metastatic cells from this tumour:
fact: Portal venous drainage from the pancreas reaches the liver first.
mnemonic: Portal flow: pancreas to liver first.
finding: Portal venous anatomy supports liver as the first metastatic receiving organ.

stem: The lateral femoral cutaneous nerve innervates which of the following:
fact: The lateral femoral cutaneous nerve is sensory and supplies skin over the lateral thigh.

stem: The iliohypogastric nerve supplies skin over which of the following regions:
fact: The iliohypogastric nerve arises from L1 and supplies posterolateral gluteal skin.
mnemonic: Iliohypogastric: L1 to lateral gluteal skin.
finding: NCBI confirms L1 origin and posterolateral gluteal supply.

stem: Which of the following is the most common position of the vermiform appendix:
fact: The retrocaecal position is the most common position of the appendix, followed by pelvic.
finding: Standard appendix anatomy supports the displayed retrocaecal key.

stem: A 49 year old man presents to ED with a few months history of abdominal pain, weight loss and jaundice. Imaging shows a tumour in the uncinate process of the pancreas. Which of the following structures is most likely compressed by this tumour:
fact: The uncinate process lies posterior to the superior mesenteric vessels.
finding: NCBI pancreatic relations support the superior mesenteric artery option.

stem: The lymphatics of the glans penis drain primarily to which of the following lymph nodes:
fact: Lymphatics from the glans penis drain primarily to the deep inguinal nodes.
finding: NCBI explicitly identifies deep inguinal drainage from the glans penis.

stem: Pain in the jejunum and ileum is typically referred to which of the following regions:
fact: Jejunal and ileal midgut visceral pain is referred to the periumbilical region.
mnemonic: Midgut pain is around the umbilicus.
finding: Midgut anatomy and source explanation support the umbilical region.

stem: A 75 year old man presents to ED complaining of abdominal pain radiating to his back, anorexia and weight loss. Imaging shows a large tumour of the neck of the pancreas. Which of the following structures is most likely compressed by the tumour:
fact: The portal vein forms posterior to the neck of the pancreas from the splenic and superior mesenteric veins.
mnemonic: Portal vein forms behind the pancreatic neck.
finding: PMC confirms portal-vein formation behind the pancreatic neck.

stem: The termination of the abdominal aorta can be visualised on the anterior abdominal wall by a point:
options: Halfway between the xiphisternum and the umbilicus
Halfway between the umbilicus and the pubic symphysis
About 2.5 cm above the deep inguinal ring
fact: The abdominal aorta bifurcates into the common iliac arteries at a surface point about 2.5 cm below the umbilicus in the source teaching.
mnemonic: Aortic bifurcation: just below the umbilicus.
finding: NCBI confirms common-iliac termination; the surface landmark follows the original source and is retained as a conventional landmark caveat.
